remediation.root_cause: The fence triggers covered only the 40 FENCED_TABLES. workspace_access and local_recovery_identity had no trigger at all, so raw SQL with the SQLCipher key could, during a live fence, clear the shared 5-attempt/60s lockout, rewrite the restore generation and substitute business identity.

findings.title: Restore-boundary verifier rejects every legitimate split cash+credit retail sale and misses a deleted split-credit entry
findings.code_path: A split retail sale posts cash/UPI/card parts through payments::invoice_posted and books ONLY the credit part as customer debt via customers::post_split_credit, whose entry carries invoice_id=invoice and kind=sale with amount = credit parts (< invoice total). Because that rule never looked at retail invoices, deleting the split-credit entry was also undetected.
findings.attack_scenario: A shop that sells partly on khata cannot restore its own backup at all (availability defect), and a backup whose split-credit entry was lost silently understates customer outstanding.

remediation.fix: The reverse rule now accepts the split form as well (retail tender, credit parts equal to the entry amount, same customer). Two new forward rules make it bidirectional: a retail invoice must have exactly one kind=sale entry iff its credit parts are non-zero, and that entry must equal the recorded credit parts for the invoice customer. findings.title: The PostgreSQL replication migration is not re-runnable
findings.code_path: Every object used a bare CREATE (tables, index, view, policies). applyReplicationMigration simply executes the file, so a retried deploy or a second call against an already-migrated database aborts.
findings.attack_scenario: A deploy retry, a rolled-forward environment, or any second apply of the migration fails partway, leaving the operator to hand-repair the schema.
findings.expected_invariant: Applying the migration twice must be a no-op and must leave exactly one of every object.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Round 1 OK, round 2 fails 42P07 relation "businesses" already exists.
findings.impact: Operational: recovery from a failed deploy requires manual DBA intervention.

findings.title: Cloud ingest rejects the second envelope of every real desktop retail sale because operation identity omits the stream
findings.code_path: A desktop retail sale writes ONE operationId to two outboxes: local_retail_outbox (stream=retail) and local_billing_outbox (stream=billing) — CheckoutPanel.tsx reuses request.operationId for the retail action, payments.rs::post_retail stores it, and replication_matrix_tests.rs proves the native export emits both (bill-cash-upi is billing seq 5 and retail seq 3). PostgreSQL scopes identity as (business_id, restore_generation, stream, operation_id) and postgres.ts dedups with stream, but store.ts and ingest.ts keyed store.byOperation by `${businessId}|${operationId}` and hydrateFromPostgres did the same.
findings.attack_scenario: Every genuine retail sale paid by UPI, card, cash+UPI, cash+card or cash+credit fails to replicate: the first (retail) envelope commits, then the billing envelope of the SAME commit is matched against the retail payload, its payloadSha256 differs, and ingest throws CONFLICT. The sale never reaches the cloud projection, so the shop reports and khata silently diverge from the PC. Separately, hydrateFromPostgres overwrites the retail entry with the billing entry, so post-restart duplicate detection compares a billing payload with a retail envelope.
findings.expected_invariant: Operation identity must be (business, stream, operation), the same key the durable schema uses; two envelopes of one commit must both commit and each retry must stay idempotent with its own cursor.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Candidate: retail envelope accepted, billing envelope => ReplicationError CONFLICT; after hydration only one byOperation entry exists for the shared id; the native SQLCipher export of seven real sales contains exactly these shared ids and cannot be replicated.
findings.impact: Critical: silent loss of the cloud copy of the majority of real retail sales, and a false CONFLICT that a retrying publisher cannot resolve. It was masked because the synthetic fixtures used distinct bill-N and sale-N ids.
findings.recommended_remediation: Put the stream into the in-memory operation key everywhere (ingest, clone, hydration) and add a real shared-id fixture.

remediation.root_cause: The in-memory dedup key was narrower than the durable key: it dropped the stream dimension that the native outboxes genuinely use.
remediation.fix: CloudStore.operationKey(businessId, stream, operationId) is now the single source of the identity string; ingestEnvelope uses it for both lookup and insert, clone() rebuilds byOperation from the copy's own event log with it, and hydrateFromPostgres derives it from the stored row stream. The cross-generation dedup decision of P5-ADV-009 is unchanged: restore_generation is still deliberately excluded. The contract document and the harness source assertion were updated to the corrected identity, and a real shared-id fixture was added to both the in-memory and the durable suites.
remediation.verification: In-memory: verify:replication => 139 checks passed, exit 0, including both envelopes committing, both retries returning their own original cursor, the clone preserving both, and a changed payload still CONFLICT. Durable on real PostgreSQL 16.2: verify:replication-postgres => 79 checks passed, including two event rows for the shared id, independent cursors, hydration keeping both stream identities and the same-payload-conflict rejection. Native: verify:replication-native-https => 123 checks passed over the real SQLCipher export that contains shared ids.

items.title: rotatePublisherGeneration was exported from postgres.ts but not from the package entry point, had no caller, and had no test
items.root_cause: Not a missing export: the operation was also UNSAFE to publish as it stood. It silently did nothing when the business was unknown, when no live publisher existed, and when the target generation equalled the current one (the UPDATE matched zero rows and resolved). Its result was void. Exporting it as-is would have published a restore step that can report success without having rotated anything.
items.intended_public_api: Yes. Enrollment, revocation and generation rotation are the three privileged server-side operations of a restore. enrollPrivileged and revokePrivileged were already exported; rotation is the missing third and is required for any restore that must reach the cloud under a new generation.
items.production_consumers: No in-repo caller exists: there is no HTTP route for enrollment/rotation (https.ts serves /v1/replication/ingest only), and the desktop publisher rotates via DesktopPublisher.onRestore against its sidecar. The operation is therefore an operator/tooling surface applied directly to PostgreSQL, which is exactly why its failure modes had to be explicit rather than silently inert.
items.safety_analysis: It moves a transport epoch, never business identity: it writes only devices.restore_generation for one non-revoked publisher. It cannot change an operation id, a stream, a sequence or a payload, so cross-generation dedup, stream-scoped identity, cursor behaviour and conflict detection are unaffected - all four are re-asserted at 100 durable checks.
items.resolution: Hardened and exported: generation format validated against the column CHECK (INVALID_ENVELOPE); unknown business UNAUTHENTICATED; no active publisher FORBIDDEN; re-issuing the current generation CONFLICT; the device row is locked FOR UPDATE; the call returns {businessId, generation, previousGeneration, deviceId} so a caller cannot mistake a no-op for a rotation. Exported from index.ts beside enroll/revoke, with API-surface, lifecycle and refusal tests.

items.title: The duplicate-operation lookup could not use any uniqueness index and degraded to a sequential scan
items.root_cause: Semantic identity is (business_id, stream, operation_id) and deliberately excludes restore_generation, while every physical unique constraint on events leads with business_id, restore_generation. No index could serve the lookup.

measured_before.plan: Seq Scan, one row returned, N-1 filtered

items.resolution: Added CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_operation_identity (business_id, stream, operation_id, event_pk) to the re-runnable schema file. Additive: no constraint, predicate, policy or identity changed. event_pk is a key column, not an INCLUDE payload, so the 'earliest event wins' ORDER BY is satisfied by index order and the Sort node disappears.

measured_after.plan: Index Scan, flat in table size

alternatives_measured.identity_include_payload: 0.025 ms but 29 MB - rejected as redundant

items.write_cost: 20k-row single-transaction insert: 145 ms with the index vs 150 ms without (inside noise)

migration_safety.rollback: DROP INDEX restores the old plan, rows intact

verification: shipped schema at 200k events: 0.033 ms indexed vs 18.88 ms with the index dropped
items.residual: Benchmark is a warm-cache, single-client, synthetic measurement on a sandbox: representative of plan shape and relative cost, not production latency. A very large existing table needs CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY out of band (documented, not automated).

iv2_003.defect: rotatePublisherGeneration read the device row and then issued an unconditional UPDATE with no transaction. Two restores could both read gen-A, both report success with previousGeneration gen-A, and leave the row on whichever UPDATE landed last.
iv2_003.fix: One explicit BEGIN/COMMIT on the handed-in connection: lock the business row, then the publisher row (the same order as ingestDurable, so they cannot deadlock), then UPDATE ... WHERE restore_generation = $2 RETURNING. Zero rows means CONFLICT. 40001/40P01 are retried at most 3 times, then surfaced as CONFLICT; no raw driver error escapes.
iv2_003.no_pool: SqlDatabase is connection-scoped; there is no pg.Pool anywhere in packages/, scripts/ or apps/.
iv2_003.new_tests: 5 concurrency cases on separate pg.Client connections: same-target race (exactly one commit, loser CONFLICT), different-target race (a genuine chain from the start generation, never an assumed order), same-generation retry, rotation racing a real ingestDurable, and the opposite-order lock probe.
iv2_003.mutation_proof: Reverting postgres.ts to b735789 and re-running the suite fails 6/6 with 'the two transitions form a real chain from the start (["race-gen-C"])' and 'exactly one concurrent rotation to the same generation commits (2 of 2)'.
assertions_deliberately_not_made: A fixed commit order for racing rotations (the one issued first can commit second).
A single expected error code for an ingest that loses the race: GAP and STALE_GENERATION are both correct fail-closed outcomes.

iv2_004.defect: The index, plan and 775x measurement lived in a document plus two bench scripts that nothing in npm run verify ran. A later change could drop or reshape the index and every gate stayed green.
iv2_004.fix: verify:replication-postgres asserts, inside one always-rolled-back transaction on a dedicated connection: both composite UNIQUE constraints still lead with restore_generation; the index is exactly (business_id, stream, operation_id, event_pk) and never restore_generation; the lookup for an operation behind a 40k-row backlog is index-served and examines <= 4 rows; dropping the index degrades the same lookup to O(table) rows; re-applying the migration restores the index and the fast plan; the rollback leaves zero probe rows and the index present.

columns reordered to (business_id, operation_id, stream, event_pk) -> identity check fails

iv2_004.not_claimed: Plan shape is the gate; timing is asserted only as a relative inequality, and the warm-cache single-client limitation stands.
